'''Sir Robert Raphael Hayim Jacob''', [[Privy Council of the United Kingdom|PC]] (born 26 April 1941), known as '''Robin Jacob''', is a former [[Lord Justice of Appeal|judge]] in the [[Court of Appeal of England and Wales]].<ref>Judiciary of England and Wales, [http://www.judiciary.gov.uk/about-the-judiciary/judges-magistrates-and-tribunal-judges/list-of-members-of-the-judiciary/senior-judiciary-list.htm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313141606/http://www.judiciary.gov.uk/about-the-judiciary/judges-magistrates-and-tribunal-judges/list-of-members-of-the-judiciary/senior-judiciary-list.htm |date=13 March 2012 }}, 4 May 2011, not yet updated to reflect his retirement.</ref>

== Personal life ==
Jacob's father was Sir Jack Jacob, a Senior Master of the [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] who is well known for editing the White Book on [[Civil procedure in England and Wales|civil procedure]] in the UK.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Glasser|first=Cyril|date=2001-01-01|title=Obituaries: Sir Jack Jacob|url=http://www.theguardian.com/news/2001/jan/01/guardianobituaries1|access-date=2021-04-26|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref>

==Education and professional career==
He read Natural Sciences (physics) at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] (1960–1963) and law at the [[London School of Economics]] (1963–1967). He was called to the bar by [[Gray's Inn]] in 1965 (Treasurer 2007). From 1976 to 1981, he was the Junior Counsel for the Comptroller of Patents and for Government departments in intellectual property.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Comparative Legal Guides|url=https://iclg.com/firms/8-new-square/robin-jacob|access-date=2020-06-16|website=International Comparative Legal Guides International Business Reports|language=en}}</ref> He took [[Queen's Counsel|silk]] in 1981. In 1993, he was appointed a [[High Court judge (England and Wales)|High Court judge]] (a designated Patent Judge) and to the [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeal]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.8newsquare.co.uk/members-of-chambers/Rt.Hon.+Professor+Sir+Robin+Jacob++ |title=8 New Square - Rt.Hon. Professor Sir Robin Jacob |access-date=24 May 2014 |archive-date=25 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140525233329/http://www.8newsquare.co.uk/members-of-chambers/Rt.Hon.+Professor+Sir+Robin+Jacob++ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His primary area of expertise is intellectual property rights.  He was admitted to the IP Hall of Fame in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iphalloffame.com/inductees/2006/Robin_Jacob.aspx|title = Robin Jacob – iphalloffame}}</ref> He was awarded the Outstanding Achievement in IP award by MIP in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2012|url=https://www.managingipawards.com/2012|access-date=2020-06-16|website=Managing IP Awards 2020|language=en-US}}</ref> The position he held before includes member of the Scientific and advisory board of the European Patent Office and the European Commission's Expert Group on the development and implications of patent law in the field of biotechnology and genetic engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Comparative Legal Guides|url=https://iclg.com/firms/8-new-square/robin-jacob|access-date=2020-06-16|website=International Comparative Legal Guides International Business Reports|language=en}}</ref> He is the President of the Intellectual Property Judges’ Association (the association of European IP, particularly patent, judges) and the chairman of the advisory board concerning appointment and training of Judges to the Preparatory Committee for the [[Unified Patent Court]] (and also a member of the committee's Expert Panel).<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Comparative Legal Guides|url=https://iclg.com/firms/8-new-square/robin-jacob|access-date=2020-06-16|website=International Comparative Legal Guides International Business Reports|language=en}}</ref>

He retired from the Court of Appeal in March 2011 (acknowledged in a valedictory address<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.iposgoode.ca/wp-content/uploads/2011/03/Valedictory_LORD_JUSTICE_JACOB_2011_Mar_22.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=4 May 2011 |archive-date=25 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725143155/http://www.iposgoode.ca/wp-content/uploads/2011/03/Valedictory_LORD_JUSTICE_JACOB_2011_Mar_22.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> before a court-room packed with well-wishers) to take up his current position as the [[Hugh Laddie|Sir Hugh Laddie]] Chair in Intellectual Property Law at the [https://www.ucl.ac.uk/ibil/ Institute of Brand and Innovation Law (IBIL)], [[University College London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/laws/ibil/index.shtml|title=Institute of Brand and Innovation Law|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012211941/http://www.ucl.ac.uk/laws/ibil/index.shtml|archive-date=2016-10-12|url-status=dead|access-date=2023-08-14}}</ref> However, in accordance with [http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1981/54/section/9 section 9] of the [[Senior Courts Act 1981]], he has continued on occasion since that date to sit as a judge in the High Court and the Court of Appeal until April 2015. Jacob is currently a [[door tenant]] at 8 New Square Chambers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.8newsquare.co.uk/members-of-chambers/index.html |title=Members of Chambers |access-date=20 July 2012 |archive-date=19 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120719110412/http://www.8newsquare.co.uk/members-of-chambers/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2018, Jacob took up the post of a Justice at the [[Astana International Financial Centre]] in the capital of Kazakhstan.<ref>{{cite web |title=UK royal judge to head AIFC |url=https://www.inform.kz/en/uk-royal-judge-to-head-aifc_a3145751 |website=Kazinform|date=7 February 2018 }}</ref>

== Selected cases in which Jacob appeared as counsel ==
* [[Interlego AG v Tyco Industries Inc|Interlego AG v Tyco Industries (Hong Kong)]] [1988] UKPC 3 - in which he successfully argued that designs for [[Lego]]'s bricks were not protected by copyright
* Smith Kline & French Laboratories v Evans Medical [1989] 1 FSR 561 - in which it was held that private acts can infringe upon a patent if they are done for commercial purposes
* Lux Traffic Controls v Pike Signals [1993] RPC 107 - it was held that a prototype tested publicly such that an observer would be able be to figure out how it worked would be disclosed, and thus constitute prior art

==Judgments==
=== High Court ===
* Henry Brothers (Magherafelt) Ltd v Ministry of Defence [1997] RPC 693 - concerning a patent for a prefabricated blast-proof building designed for use in Northern Ireland during [[the Troubles]]
* ''[http://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWHC/Patents/1999/226.html Mars UK v Teknowledge]'' [1999] EWHC 226 (Pat) - where he held that the mere fact of encryption will not make information confidential for the purposes of the action for [[Breach of confidence in English law|breach of confidence]]

=== Court of Appeal ===
*''[[Walton v Independent Living Organisation]]'' [2003] EWCA Civ 199, [2003] ICR 688, [2003] IRLR 469 - [[UK labour law]], regarding the [[National Minimum Wage Act 1998]]
*''[https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2004/159.html Reed Executive Plc & Anor v Reed Business Information Ltd & Ors]'' [2004] EWCA Civ 159 - UK [[United Kingdom trade mark law|trademark law]], on the test of confusion
*''[https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2005/565.html Hyperion Records v Dr Lionel Sawkins]'' [2005] EWCA Civ 565 - concerning copyright in unfinished works by [[Michel Richard Delalande|Lalande]] that had been completed by the claimant
*''[https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2006/145.html IDA v University of Southampton]'' [2006] EWCA Civ 145 - concerning a patent for a cockroach trap
*''[https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2007/588.html Pozzoli SPA v BDMO SA and others]'' [2007] FSR 37 - he set out the prevailing test for [[Inventive step and non-obviousness|inventive step]], reformulating the test set out by [[Peter Oliver, Baron Oliver of Aylmerton|Oliver LJ]] in the ''[[Windsurfing#Patents|Windsurfing]]'' case
*''[[Aerotel Ltd v Telco Holdings Ltd]]'' [2007] RPC 7 - UK patent law, regarding the excluded subject-matter (software) in the UK patent law
*''[http://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2008/192.html European Central Bank v Document Security Systems]'' [2007] EWCA Civ 192 - notable for the graphical illustration of the importance of consistency in interpreting patent claims in relation to validity and infringement:<blockquote>... Professor Mario Franzosi likens a patentee to an [[Angora cat]]. When validity is challenged, the patentee says his patent is very small: the cat with its fur smoothed down, cuddly and sleepy. But when the patentee goes on the attack, the fur bristles, the cat is twice the size with teeth bared and eyes ablaze.</blockquote>
*''[https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2007/936.html Procter & Gamble Co v Reckitt Benckiser (UK) Ltd]'' [2007] EWCA Civ 936 - UK [[Design right (United Kingdom)|design law]]
*Jacob gave the leading judgment in ''[[DWF LLP]] v [[Secretary of State for Business Innovation and Skills]]'' (acting for the [[Insolvency Service]]), "at the invitation of [[Arden LJ]]".<ref>Sir Robin Jacob, [https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2014/900.html DWF LLP v Secretary of State for Business Innovation and Skills <nowiki>[</nowiki>2014<nowiki>]</nowiki> EWCA Civ 900], delivered on 8 July 2014, accessed on 29 July 2025</ref>
